payload.reason: The evidence provides specific information about the improvements in accuracy of the Attention-Sum Reader model when trained on the BookTest dataset compared to the Children's Book Test (CBT).

claims.text: Training on the BookTest dataset improves the accuracy of the Attention-Sum Reader model on the CBT test data by a much larger margin than many recent attempts to improve model architecture.
Training on the new dataset reduces the prediction error by almost one third, bringing the model's performance to the level of the human baseline on the named-entity version of CBT.
Moving model training from CBT to a subset of the BookTest results in a drop in accuracy of around 10% on the CBT test datasets, indicating the importance of data selection.
